questions.q: What does Grafana need before it can build any panels against Prometheus?
options: A separate copy of the TSDB
A data source configured with a name and the Prometheus server's URL
A rewritten version of every PromQL query in Grafana's own syntax
Alertmanager must be installed first
questions.explain: Grafana queries Prometheus's HTTP API through a data source, which just needs a name and the server's URL (e.g. http://localhost:9090). The same PromQL you already know works unchanged once that connection exists.

options: A separate Prometheus server dedicated to one dashboard
One visualization on a dashboard, wrapping one or more PromQL queries with a chosen chart type
A type of exporter
A Kubernetes object that stores alert rules
questions.explain: A panel is a single visualization — a time series graph, single stat, table, etc. — built from one or more queries against a data source, and a dashboard is a grid of these panels.

questions.q: Why would Northbridge put a Grafana dashboard in front of on-call engineers instead of relying on the Prometheus expression browser during an incident?
options: The expression browser can't run PromQL queries at all
A Grafana dashboard persists and can be shared by URL, so the whole on-call rotation looks at the same view instead of retyping queries
Grafana dashboards don't require a data source
The expression browser is only available during business hours
questions.explain: The expression browser is stateless — close the tab and the query is gone. A saved Grafana dashboard persists, can be shared by URL, and lets a whole team look at the same panels during an incident.

questions.q: Which PromQL query would best power a 'p95 checkout latency' panel?
options: checkout_requests_total
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(checkout_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))
up{job="checkout"}
sum(checkout_requests_total)
questions.explain: histogram_quantile() applied to the rate of a histogram's bucket counts is exactly how you calculate a percentile like p95 latency — this is the standard pattern from Lesson 16 applied to a dashboard panel.

questions.q: What does a dashboard variable let you do?
options: Permanently change the underlying metric names in the TSDB
Let one dashboard template serve many services, by swapping a value like a service name without editing each query
Bypass the need for a data source
Convert a counter metric into a gauge
questions.explain: A dashboard variable acts as a reusable placeholder — for example, switching which service's metrics a dashboard displays — so you don't need to build and maintain a separate dashboard per service.
